subject: Re: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification — GPU type & throughput targets
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity follow-up — GPU type, throughput & pricing targets

Hi Alex — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we can align pricing options: 

- Expected token volume: 250M–1.2B tokens/month (peaks during business hours)
- Primary workload: multi-turn clinical summarization + search reranking; average generation length ~150 tokens, with many short 20–40 token calls for metadata extraction
- Target unit economics: Atlas is looking for a ballpark of $150–$250 per 1M tokens for production (goal is <$200/1M if possible)
- Throughput targets: sustained 10–15K tokens/sec during peak windows, with ability to handle 200–300 concurrent short requests with p50 latency <120ms
- Preferred GPU families: you called out interest in H100 for latency/throughput headroom, but asked for A100 comparisons if it materially reduces cost
- Reserved capacity ask: initial commit for 4–8 GPUs, with the ability to add burst capacity for events

Next steps I recommend: 
1) I’ll pull together two dedicated capacity pricing scenarios (4x H100 reserved and 8x A100 reserved) with estimated unit economics and expected sustained throughput. See attached pricing workbook (atlas_mup_v2_estimate.xlsx) for my working assumptions.
2) Marcus — can you validate the throughput assumptions and add any kernel/quantization notes we should propose?
3) Alex — if the $/1M targets above are in the right ballpark, let me know and I’ll get legal/procurement-ready pricing + a one-page tech appendix.

If helpful we can do a 30-min follow up Thursday to walk the workbook.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0187

Attachments: atlas_mup_v2_estimate.xlsx (pricing assumptions), redwood-dedicated-pricing.pdf (reference sheet)

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@atlashealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@atlashealth.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 17:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity follow-up — GPU type, throughput & pricing targets

Thanks Marissa — this is really helpful. A few clarifications from my side: 

- Volume: 250M–1.2B/month is accurate; first 3 months we expect closer to 300–400M as we ramp pilots across 3 hospitals
- Unit economics: our budget team is targeting ~ $175/1M tokens for the committed capacity line item; we could accept up to $220/1M if it includes stronger SLA and dedicated support
- GPU preference: H100 preferred for the latency-sensitive summarization workload, but we asked to see A100 for cost comparison
- Minimum reserved: we are comfortable with a 6-GPU initial commit (we mentioned 4–8 in the call) — 6 gives us headroom for redundancy and rolling updates

Procurement asked if you can provide two line-item quotes: (A) 6x H100 reserved, 12-month term; (B) 6x A100 reserved, 12-month term — each with estimated $/1M token guidance and expected sustained throughput (tokens/sec) under our workload. Please include any assumptions around batching, KV cache hit rates, or quantization that materially change cost.

Appreciate it — can we target having the quote by end-of-day Thursday?

Best,
Alex
Director, AI Platforms | Atlas Health
alex.rivera@atlashealth.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 08:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity follow-up — GPU type, throughput & pricing targets

Looping in a quick technical note for the pricing scenarios: 

- For Atlas’s workload (multi-turn, 150-token averages with many short calls), H100 nets ~1.6–2.0x the sustained tokens/sec compared to A100 when using large-context models with KV cache enabled. That typically reduces required reserved GPUs by ~30–40% for the same p50 latency.
- If Atlas is willing to accept 8-bit quantization for some model variants, you can reduce cost further — conservatively a 20% improvement in tokens/$ for generation workloads; we should call out quality tradeoffs.
- Assumptions I used in the workbook: 60% cache hit rate (prefix reuse), batching efficiency 65% during peaks, and model family X-70 (open checkpoint) with optimized kernels.

I’ll update the workbook with expected sustained tokens/sec for both 6x H100 and 6x A100 and a per-1M token cost estimate (including reserved infra amortized over 12 months + support).

—Marcus
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@atlashealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity follow-up — Dedicated pricing & next steps

Hi Alex — thanks for the fast response and the budget target. I’ve attached the formal two-option quote (redwood-dedicated-pricing.pdf) and an updated workbook that includes the per-1M token estimates under Marcus’s throughput assumptions. Highlights: 

- Option A (6x H100, 12 mo): estimated $165/1M tokens (assuming 60% cache hit, 65% batching) — sustained ~12–16K tokens/sec; p50 latency ~90–110ms for median requests
- Option B (6x A100, 12 mo): estimated $210/1M tokens — sustained ~7–9K tokens/sec; p50 latency ~140–180ms
- Bursting: both options include configurable burst to shared pool up to additional 4 GPUs (best-effort) for spikes; formalized in appendix
- SLA: 99.9% uptime, dedicated support channel + 8x5 phone support included for the reserved plan

Next steps: 
1) Review the two-option PDF and the workbook (links attached).
2) If either option aligns with procurement, we’ll produce a draft order form and SOW for signature.
3) We’re available Thurs 3/19 10:00–11:00 PT for a quick walk-through — want me to lock that?

If helpful, I can also include a sensitivity table showing $/1M with different cache hit and batching assumptions.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Engagement Manager | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
